body.statement: For each equality certificate at \(n=2,4,6\), the full-count posterior mean under the least-favorable prior is constant on every positive-predictive-mass \(W\)-fiber, and a scalar completion controls every remaining state. At \(n=8\), the certified full rule is not constant on the fiber \(W=2\), since \(t_8(1,0)=73084/10^6\) and \(t_8(2,1)=152579/10^6\), while Theorem 4 places its full-count worst risk below a lower bound valid for every \(W\)-rule. Thus the second count first changes the minimax envelope through failure of the scalar saddle equations, not through ordinary posterior relevance alone.
body.justification: The proposition isolates the decision-theoretic mechanism behind the first strict threshold.
body.gap: Blackwell's experiment order does not characterize equality for one target and one loss, while the published minimax papers do not inspect these fixed-half posterior fibers.
body.consumer: Analysts can distinguish a statistic that is posterior-informative from one whose discarded information actually changes worst-case optimal risk.
